reason: Closed in the dense-core review because the pseudo-reduction's boundary-expansion and bounded row-weight hypotheses fail for blocks of dense clauses. That is an inapplicability the attempt found, not a one-step remark. The lead's other target, a gluing base that tolerates falls, moved to the Mikša–Nordström operator (Theorem 4.9) lead, which the closure and relative reviews developed into the relative criterion. So the idea is carried there.

The lead's target was an upper bound on perm(omega^A) giving joint equidistribution of a block's restricted constants. lem:swap-decay and cor:dense-shift-equidistribution prove this for every nonzero combination that is far from additive. The target is met by a proved result. The closing phrase 'stalls at the missing global mechanism' concerns the downstream use, which the renormalization-group bridge carries (reopened).

The flow is proved block by block (swap decay). The bridge was closed only because 'the line lacks a global mechanism'. That is not a reason the attempt found, and the universality step, from adversarial dense blocks to a semi-random residual, was never attempted. The current A1 next step uses a partial matching rho drawn after the prefixes and a restricted matching design nu_rho, which is exactly the coarse-graining step this bridge models. A1 also points random tops to A3-type Taylor conditions, which a semi-random reduction would feed.
open_statement: A1 (dense core: local designs / restricted matching design nu_rho)
next_attempt: Combine cor:dense-shift-equidistribution with the few-columns next step. For rho drawn after the prefixes, state the semi-random residual (residual linear parts with independent uniform shifts) and decide whether nu_rho kills every degree-at-most-D function supported in one shifted block's excluded set. First check whether uniform constant shifts affect anything at the level of A3's top conditions. If the tops are shift-independent, close as inapplicable.

reason: Its sole target was a decay rate for |perm(omega^A)|/N! by interaction pattern. lem:swap-decay proved an explicit decay bound in terms of distance from additive, which is all the reduction uses. This is supersession by a proved result. Exact cavity rates have no open statement that needs them.

It was developed into lem:relative-criterion and prop:semantic-local-kill, which prove the operator as a base on boundary expanders. The remaining gluing question was transferred explicitly to the Mikša–Nordström closure lead. The item was developed to its target, and its continuation is carried elsewhere.

The descent rule R(xR(t))=R(xt), with a degree-filtered projection, was proved as lem:relative-criterion. The lead's whole content, a relative closure criterion, is now a working proof. No further application of the descent itself is named.

The bridge asked only how prevalent blocked centres are. Its mean-field prediction matched the random board (112.4 against 112), and blocked centres were shown to be generic on W's boards. The closure-relative base absorbs their falls. The question is answered, and the translation has no other target.

Over several reviews the budget became the pointwise W_RS error bound and the Kotecky–Preiss bridge. It was closed as merged into Kotecky–Preiss, which carries its question (smallness absorbing many blocks). That is supersession by a carrier item. The carrier, Kotecky–Preiss, is reopened in this batch, so the idea is not lost.

The test proved that flat weights cost exactly 2q (the unique point-indicator over F_3 has degree 2m), and this was used in the replay barrier's counting. The lead's question, whether conditioning's cost of 2 per form is forced, is settled for its translation. Weights of other shapes fall outside the theorem's hypotheses. Conditioning itself is capped (weighted-replay barrier), so no open statement uses the bound further.

The SoS-lead entry was a three-minute assessment without re-reading the paper. It closed the lead because cube-variable expansion, harmless linear structure and positivity fail on dense blocks. It examined only the absorption of n^K constraints through expansion. It did not examine the later use that the tests had already supplied: t-wise uniform measures on a W clause's allowed patterns (found by exact LP for k=3,4,5). Measures on each block's allowed set are exactly the local designs of prop:local-design-criterion, which A1 now names as the route beyond capacity.
open_statement: A1 (local designs: a measure on each block's allowed set)
next_attempt: Read KMOW's planted-distribution construction in full. Test whether F_3-valued t-wise uniform measures on a block's allowed set (from the recorded LP, reduced mod 3 where 3-integral) can serve as the per-block measures of prop:local-design-criterion, agreeing up to degree D with a weak-PHP design functional. Do this at the smallest size where the few-columns review's nu_rho test is run.

reason: Its target was sparse conditioning for adversarial blocks at K below 1, and the test (nonzero permanent about 4/9 of the time) passed. It was closed because the permanent condition matters only below the conditioning budget, and the record proves that budget is capped at about n/10 surviving blocks with product weights. That is an inapplicability to the goal's K at least 1, not a one-step remark.

It was closed because 'its smallness surrogate, the integrality line, is parked'. The integrality line, in turn, was parked (lem:auxiliary-bit-relaxation) for lack of 'a characteristic-0 many-block mechanism', which is precisely what this bridge proposes. The closure is circular and no reason was found by an attempt. lem:auxiliary-bit-relaxation makes a 3-integral char-0 design of PHP plus encoded blocks reduce, block by block, to an F_3 design. The 3-integrality of a cluster expansion was recorded as untested and never tested.
open_statement: A1 (dense core; every certificate needs a Nullstellensatz design)
next_attempt: Build the rational cluster expansion around the integral PHP design (thm:integral-design-extension) for weak PHP plus a few aux-bit-encoded dense blocks, with each block a polymer, and check the Kotecky–Preiss criterion. Then test at the smallest informative size (6 pigeons, NS degree 3, one or two encoded blocks) whether the truncated cluster sums are 3-integral and reduce to an F_3 design.

reason: It was closed because the only passed test was tautological at q=1 and the analogy 'predicts nothing beyond'. That is a one-step remark: the multi-sector analogue predicts a checkable condition, sparse conditioning for q at least 2 equations iff every nonzero combination is non-confined, and this was never tested. Its relevance to the current open statements is unclear, because conditioning is capped at about n/10 blocks and the n^K-sector statement may just restate A1.
open_statement: A1 (many dense blocks jointly invisible to low-degree operators)
next_attempt: Test the multi-charge prediction at small boards: for q=2,3 equations, check whether the doubled-permanent condition fails exactly when some nonzero F_3-combination is confined. Then decide whether a topological-order local-indistinguishability theorem gives anything for n^K sectors beyond restating A1.

reason: The randomization became thm:randomized-prefix-reduction and is now the open statement W_RS itself, the sufficient weakening listed under W, together with prop:bounded-column-vacuity and the light-family results. Its limit was made explicit: it randomizes coefficients, not linear parts. The idea now is the framework of the open statements rather than a pending lead, so no further development remains for the item itself.

Closed because all W_RS proofs use averaging over C, and existence of prefixes is what W_RS needs. The lemma adds two-sided concentration of the error density, and only the upper side is ever useful, which Markov already gives. The test also showed that the min-entropy (3.54 bits) is far below the 14.3 needed. This is an inapplicability the attempt found.

It was carried as Continuing for four reviews and then closed by the same SoS-lead assessment. The paper was not re-read, and only expansion-based absorption in cube variables was examined. The test found pairwise-uniform distributions on the allowed value vectors of randomized blocks. Under W_RS these are candidate per-block measures for local designs, and the A1 next step is set exactly in W_RS (rho chosen after the prefixes).
open_statement: A1 under W_RS (local designs on randomized blocks' allowed sets)
next_attempt: For random C_b with t=2,3 at small h, compute F_3-valued (or 3-integral) t-wise uniform measures on each block's allowed set. Test whether they extend to a local design in the sense of prop:local-design-criterion together with the weak-PHP matching design, starting with a single block and then two blocks sharing linear parts.

reason: It was used twice. For W_RS clause consistency it gave only the trivial degree bound, and on the bad locus of thm:generic-top-directness it gave only an exponentially small fraction of good points. Both were found by the attempt. Against the current local-design step, a nonzero degree-D function is nonzero on at least a 2^{-D} fraction of the cube, with D=22k, far below the 3^{-t} density of an excluded set. So the theorem cannot exclude low-degree functions supported there.

It was used in the union bounds of pinned rank vacuity and occupancy pinning. The bridge's own text records that the link from few forbidden points to no low-degree refutation is the open core restated. prop:thinness-equivalence and the few-columns review later showed that density alone cannot give the design. The item was developed and its remaining content is a restatement.

It was closed with no work because the random-form line was parked, which is not a reason an attempt found. The test (MeatAxe absolute irreducibility at five parameter sets) passed. The break, Nenashev's generic-tuple step having no analogue for F_3-points, was never attacked. The current A3 status cites generic directness for random tops, and A1 needs A3-type Taylor conditions for random tops, so a rational (F_3-point) directness statement still bears on open statements.
open_statement: A3 (random tops: generic directness at F_3-points), feeding A1's random-top certificate half
next_attempt: Use the verified absolute irreducibility of the modules A_j (tilde) under G(F_3) to replace the generic-tuple step. Try a G(F_3)-orbit argument showing that the directness minor's nonvanishing set meets a constant fraction of F_3-points, and check it exactly for z=2 tops at (m,N)=(2,4),(2,5).

reason: It was developed into prop:pinned-rank-vacuity and prop:occupancy-pin-reduction, both working proofs, for families sharing few linear parts. The item was developed to its scope, and a recorded cap covers its extension.

It was closed with no work because it serves the parked random-form line. Its test showed that two-top orbit types (171 atom types) are polynomially many, which would reduce the rational two-top directness question to type densities. Its value depends on whether rational directness for random tops (reopened in the absolute-irreducibility item) is pursued. The record does not decide this.

next_attempt: Use the 171 GL_2(3) atom types to compute the exact directness bad fraction for m=2 pairs over orbit representatives at small N, as a test of the rational directness item.

reason: It motivated measuring sharing by rank modulo a shared part, which prop:pinned-rank-vacuity uses, and that line is complete. Its test was the same algebraic identity as the falsification, with no independent prediction left. It was developed to exhaustion within its scope.

reason: It was developed in the slot Hilbert entry, which measured the graded ring of the arrangement complement in the cube. The complement keeps almost all dimensions, closing the per-slot count, and the DAG review closed the joint count. These are falsifications found by computation and recorded in the remaining route ('subspace criterion gives nothing at p=3, per slot or jointly').

It was developed in the Brauer-count entry, which found that an invariant family of orbit equalities keeps the fixed-point instance as hard as the original. So no degree transfer exists for invariant axiom sets in general. This is a falsification found by the development cycle, not a one-step remark. Adversarial W families are not P-invariant in any case.

The logical qutrit comes from 3-torsion of the functional chessboard complex. The bridge's own check showed that the weak-base survivor complex has no torsion. The Smith-normal-form bridge showed that this torsion lies in degrees no filling step uses. These are inapplicabilities found by tests, and no argument ties code distance to degree.

Its rational-degree obstruction to MOD_3 encodings was confirmed by test (degree m or m-1), and it was closed because it bounds only exact encodings in the cube variables. The auxiliary-bit encoding bypasses it, and lem:auxiliary-bit-relaxation analysed that encoding fully. This is an inapplicability found by the attempt.

It was closed only because the integrality line is parked, which is not a reason an attempt found. For plain PHP its question, integrality beyond the connectivity range, does not matter at degree 22k=Theta(log n), which is within floor((n+1)/2), where thm:integral-design-extension already gives integral designs. If the Kotecky–Preiss char-0 route is revived, torsion of the design system of PHP plus encoded blocks decides whether a rational certificate is 3-integral, and that use was never tested.
open_statement: A1 (via a 3-integral char-0 design, the Kotecky–Preiss item)
next_attempt: Compute the 3-torsion of the design system's cokernel for weak PHP with 6 pigeons at NS degree 3 plus one aux-bit-encoded dense block. Check whether it obstructs a 3-integral certificate.

reason: Its Monte Carlo test was vacuous: uniformly random coefficients already make each pigeon's contribution uniform. Its prediction, uniform residues, is cor:dense-shift-equidistribution, already proved. Closure as a restatement of a recorded result is valid.

The small-measure entry tested it as a robustness statement and found that forbidden measure does not control PC degree under both natural distributions. The structured form reduces to the recorded vacuity question. This is a falsification found by a development cycle, consistent with the later finding that point designs cannot come from density (thinness equivalence, few-columns review).

It was closed as not needed: the chain residual keeps independent 5-subsets for ordinary residual pigeons and handles the hole side with the carry chain, so no biregular model enters any proof. This is supersession by a route that avoids the need. The model's only target was the re-proof of residual lemmas.

The code was identified as the cycle code of the residual graph, with distance equal to the girth, O(log N) and constant with constant probability. So it gives no rigidity, and the route no longer needs it. This is a falsification of the bridge's prediction found by the attempt.
